solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pressure put on old college to achieve growth

indicators.note: something put on another is added after it, so this letter follows the college

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a kind of British college that no longer exists under that name
P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Leaning on a former college to make it expand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' reads as the college's expansion, but it is a medical growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small benign lump of tissue on a membrane is a growth in the medical sense.

clue.text: Trotters in pastry dishes? British lad surprisingly gets stuck in

indicators.note: gets stuck in says the rearranged letters are pushed inside the pies

parts.note: pies are pastry dishes

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn out arranged unexpectedly

explanation.surface: Pigs' feet baked in pies, which a British lad tucks into.
explanation.walkthrough: Trotters look like pigs' feet but mean horses that trot. BLAD is rearranged to BALD and set in PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebalds are horses with patches of black and white, so they are trotting animals.

clue.text: Play Oasis hit? No don't!

indicators.note: no says the following word is to be dropped from the song title

parts.note: Don't Look Back in Anger was a 1996 number-one single by the band Oasis

explanation.surface: Someone tells you not to play an Oasis song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb but is the 1956 John Osborne drama, defined as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne's 1956 drama about Jimmy Porter is a famous British stage work, a play.

clue.text: A Roman gathering in photo giving full view

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: gathering suggests the letters are collected up and put together anew

explanation.surface: A Roman crowd appears in a wide-angle photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' reads as a crowd of Romans but signals rearranging the letters of 'A Roman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in a whole wide scene, a full view.

clue.text: Watering holes, mostly cold and uncivilised

parts.note: watering holes are pubs, so one bar after another
the second of the two pub counters

indicators.note: mostly means all of the word but its last letter, so the cold word loses its tail

parts.note: icy means very cold

explanation.surface: A grumble about a run of chilly, unfriendly pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'holes' gives two bars; 'mostly' trims ICY to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric behaviour is savage and crude, the opposite of civilised conduct.

clue.text: Fear lad upset woman

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened boy is distressed by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfreda is a female first name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Timber transported by Hannibal's army

indicators.note: letters carried along by the words, like goods by an army, are concealed within them

explanation.surface: Hannibal's army hauled wood across the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in HanniBAL'S Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood from a tropical American tree, a kind of timber.

clue.text: Euro's stature nil after crash? It's a risky business

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: After a financial crash the euro's standing is zero, a risky affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'It's' are link words; the fifteen letters of EUROS STATURE NIL are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning a revolver's chamber and firing at one's own head is an extremely dangerous game, hence any reckless venture.

clue.text: German wearing extremely clean fabric

indicators.note: the outer letters wear the name, wrapping round it
extremely points to the extremities, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German dressed in spotless cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: C and N, the ends of 'clean', go around OTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is cloth woven from the fibre of the cotton plant, a common fabric.

clue.text: Kingdom of Spain enlisting private army

indicators.note: enlisting says the kingdom takes the soldier into its ranks, holding him inside

parts.note: Leon was a medieval kingdom in northern Spain
a GI is a US private soldier

explanation.surface: A Spanish kingdom recruits a private army.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit, and the word now means a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Backward individual — poor pupil head expelled, say

indicators.note: backward tells us the single-person word is written from its end to its start

parts.note: an individual is one single person

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and expelled says it is thrown out

parts.note: a dunce is a slow or poor pupil

explanation.surface: A slow pupil gets expelled, as a headteacher might announce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head expelled' sounds like a school story but simply removes the D of DUNCE, leaving UNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is a formal word meaning to pronounce or state aloud, as one might say something.

clue.text: Pages of writing found in box close to West Ealing location?

indicators.note: found in says the manuscript sits inside the box

parts.note: a box file is a filing box, so box gives file
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, pages of writing

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone finds manuscript pages in a box near West Ealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios in west London is a famous film studio, hence the question mark: a place where shooting happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing Studios is a classic British movie studio, so a shooting location there is an example of a set for movies.

clue.text: Vegetable popular in French restaurant

indicators.note: in says the popular word goes inside the restaurant word

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn or restaurant
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish that's popular at a French restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: An auberge is a country inn in France; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, called eggplant in America, is a purple vegetable.

clue.text: Friend from abroad taking a journey on motorway

indicators.note: on places the journey word after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a go can be a trip or turn, a journey

explanation.surface: A foreign friend sets off on a trip along the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway running from London to Leeds; read the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for pal, so it is a foreign word for a friend.

clue.text: Mounted action to sort paperwork

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer mounts an operation to get the paperwork in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the thirteen letters of MOUNTED ACTION are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentation is the body of papers and records supporting something, i.e. paperwork.

clue.text: I'm beaten up and incarcerated

parts.note: pounded means beaten hard

explanation.surface: A prisoner complains of being beaten and locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impounded is seized and shut away, much as a prisoner is confined.

clue.text: Vessel crossing river has trouble in part of the rigging

indicators.note: crossing says the ship straddles the river, holding it between its letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
the Tay is a river in Scotland
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A ship crossing a river has a problem with its rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a sail hoisted on a stay, one of the ropes supporting a mast, so it belongs to a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Social security payment, I note, is for discussion by the Left

parts.note: a matter that comes up is raised for discussion
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone notes that welfare benefits are being debated by left-wing politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Left' sounds political but means the nautical left, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British state benefit paid to people on low wages, a social security payment.

clue.text: Brief colleague, having received information before a battle

indicators.note: the shortened colleague takes in the information, holding it inside
brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A short-tempered workmate gets a briefing before a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts the last letter, MAT. Magenta was an 1859 battle in Italy, after which the dye was named; 'having received' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta in Lombardy was the site of an 1859 French-Austrian clash, so its name stands for that battle.

clue.text: Rap singer drooping about second part of show

indicators.note: about says the drooping word goes round the letter

parts.note: saggy means sagging or drooping

indicators.note: the second part of the word is its second letter

explanation.surface: A rapper looks tired during the second half of a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaggy is a Jamaican-American reggae and rap artist known for Boombastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy is the stage name of a well-known Jamaican-American musician who raps and sings.

clue.text: Right turn, changing direction to take in a short cut?

indicators.note: to take in means to hold inside, so the single letter goes into the rearranged letters
changing direction suggests the letters are switched round into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver turns right to take a short cut.
explanation.walkthrough: R and TURN are rearranged to RTRUN, which takes A in after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road used by drivers to dodge main-road traffic is a sort of short cut, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Panic, as marines do?

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the manner of, so as
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Asking whether marines panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as marines do' is a la RM, in the manner of the Royal Marines; 'do' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, much the same as panic.

clue.text: US College course in religion that goes over a cleric's head?

definitions.text: that goes over a cleric's head?

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: An American college course in religion that is beyond a priest's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over a cleric's head' suggests being too hard to follow; it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed hat is worn on top of a churchman's head, so it literally goes over it.

clue.text: Former student and university friend meeting over a period

parts.note: a grad is a graduate, someone who has finished studying
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A graduate and a university friend meet up over a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done gradually happens slowly, little by little across a period of time.

clue.text: Author, say, needs to have working PC

indicators.note: say signals that the writing verb is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to author a text is to write it
on means working or operating, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A writer needs a working personal computer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is not a computer but politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is slang for fashionably liberal in views, which is what politically correct can describe.

clue.text: Worried animal will go round nibbling one flowering plant

indicators.note: nibbling says the reversed words bite on, and so hold, the numeral
going round turns the pair of words to read the other way

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you, so worried gives ate
a dog is an animal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An anxious animal circles, chewing on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' as ate comes from 'what's eating you?'. 'will go round' makes GODETA, and 'nibbling' holds the numeral inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is a garden annual with satiny flowers, a kind of flowering plant.

clue.text: Scandinavian calls Reagan 'regressive'

indicators.note: regressive suggests going backwards, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them, so calls gives names
Ron is short for Ronald, the first name of US president Reagan

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian denounces President Reagan as a backward-looking politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' sounds like political criticism; here it reverses NAMES RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was a Viking from ancient Norway or Scandinavia.

clue.text: Live comfortably after start of downturn

indicators.note: after places the comfortable word behind the opening letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: well off or living well means comfortably

explanation.surface: Living comfortably despite an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or live there.
